title: Area
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: The area of a triangle is shown as half of a rectangle by cutting a paper rectangle along its diagonal, so the half has a reason. Combined shapes are split with a coloured line before any working; the circle is drawn on 1 cm squared paper.

skills.key_step: The child shows that a triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height, and uses the height at right angles to the base.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the area of a rectangle.
floor.question: Area of a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm?

representations: a paper rectangle cut along its diagonal
a triangle drawn on squared paper with its height dotted
the rule half x base x height
steps: Find the height at right angles to the base, not a slanting side.
contexts: a triangular flag for sports day

board.do: Draw a rectangle 8 by 5 and its diagonal.

board.say: What part of the rectangle is this triangle?

board.do: Ask the child for the area before you write it.

misconceptions.ask: Is the triangle the whole rectangle?
misconceptions.repair: The triangle is half of the rectangle: halve 40.

misconceptions.ask: Does that side stand at right angles to the base?
misconceptions.repair: The height is the straight-up distance, dotted at right angles.

misconceptions.ask: Are we going round the edge or covering the inside?
misconceptions.repair: Area covers the inside: half base times height.

misconceptions.ask: How many times do we halve?
Are we counting lengths or squares?
misconceptions.repair: Area is in square units: cm2.

checks.question: A triangle has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. What is its area?
A triangle has area 24 cm2 and base 8 cm. What is its height?

skills.key_step: The child splits the shape into rectangles, squares and triangles with a line, writes the two lengths of each part on it, and adds (or subtracts a cut-out).

floor.prerequisite: Finds areas of rectangles and triangles.
floor.question: Area of a triangle with base 6 cm and height 4 cm?

representations: a paper shape cut into pieces
the shape with a coloured split line and lengths on each part
a table of parts and their areas
steps: Draw a line to split the shape.
Write the length and width of each part, finding missing sides by subtracting.
Add the parts, or take away a part that is cut out.
contexts: a classroom floor with an alcove
a house wall with a roof
a garden with a path cut out

board.do: Draw a house shape: a 6 cm square with a triangle roof of height 4 cm.

board.say: What shape is this part, and what rule does it use?

board.do: Wait for triangle, half base times height.
Ask the child to write the area inside each part.

misconceptions.ask: Does your answer cover the whole shape?
misconceptions.repair: Find every part and add them.

misconceptions.ask: Is the cut-out part still there?
Is the second rectangle really 10 cm long?
misconceptions.repair: Write each part's own lengths; the overlap is counted once.

misconceptions.ask: Is the roof a rectangle or a triangle?

checks.question: A rectangle 10 cm by 6 cm has a 2 cm by 2 cm square cut out. What area is left?
A house shape is a 6 cm square with a triangle roof of base 6 cm and height 4 cm. What is its area?

skills.key_step: The child counts the whole squares inside the circle, counts the part squares and takes each as half, adds, and says the answer is an estimate.

floor.prerequisite: Counts squares to find an area.
floor.question: A shape covers 12 whole squares of 1 cm2. What is its area?

representations: a round lid traced on squared paper
whole squares ticked and part squares dotted
a table: whole, part, half of part, total
steps: Tick every whole square inside the circle.
Add the whole squares and half the part squares.

board.do: Draw a circle on squared paper.
Count the whole squares inside with the child.
Count the part squares with the child.

board.say: Is this a whole square of the circle?

board.do: Wait for the child to say part of one.
Write wholes + half the parts = about ... cm2.

misconceptions.ask: Are the part squares inside the circle at all?
misconceptions.repair: Add half of the part squares too.

misconceptions.ask: Is a part square a whole square?
misconceptions.repair: Take each part square as about a half.

misconceptions.ask: Are the corners of the box inside the circle?
misconceptions.repair: Count only squares inside the circle.

misconceptions.ask: Is every part square exactly a half?

checks.question: A circle covers 20 whole squares and 12 part squares of 1 cm2. Estimate its area.
A circle covers 30 whole squares and 10 part squares of 1 cm2. Estimate its area.
